item.title: A new class of optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The construction of optimal binary linear complementary pair (LCP) has recently attracted considerable attention in coding theory. Based on the Belov codes, this paper proposes a novel construction of optimal binary LCPs with $\theta=4$, extending our previous work on $\theta=3$. Our results not only yield abundant new optimal binary LCPs with flexible parameters, but also enable more optimal binary LCPs with smaller minimum distances.
item.dc:creator: Yansheng Wu, Jing Chen

item.title: Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL
item.description: arXiv:2611.03884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a UAV-assisted status-update system in which a rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collects updates from multiple sensors, stores the newest update of each sensor, and forwards selected buffered updates to a ground station (GS). We minimize a weighted sum of the time-average GS-side age of information (AoI) and UAV energy consumption over a finite horizon. The optimization is subject to half-duplex operation, sensor and UAV energy-causality constraints, transmission-rate and power limits, and a terminal-location constraint. Because collection changes the information age at the UAV but does not reduce the GS-side AoI until the buffered update is forwarded, mobility, collection, and forwarding decisions are coupled over time. We use a hierarchical AoI-energy actor-critic (HAE-AC) controller in which a coarse-timescale actor selects return-feasible UAV movements, while a deterministic per-slot scheduler constructs feasible collection or forwarding sets and assigns the minimum transmit power required for each scheduled transmission. In a 100-sensor deployment, HAE-AC reduces the average GS-side AoI by about 22% relative to an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark. Compared with forward-upon-collection, selective buffered forwarding reduces the number of downlink bursts by roughly 30% while increasing the number of collections per sensor by more than 23%.
item.dc:creator: Xiangjian Gao, Mohammad Moltafet, Hamid R. Sadjadpour

item.title: Making Every Edit Count: Efficient Binary Edit Correction at the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.04023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct binary codes that attain the classical Gilbert-Varshamov redundancy guarantee for a fixed number of edit errors, with deterministic polynomial-time construction, encoding, and decoding. For every fixed integer $t\ge 1$ and all sufficiently large block lengths $n$, our codes correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions in total, with redundancy at most $2t\log_2 n+O_t(1)$. All algorithms run in polynomial time in $n$ for fixed $t$, and decoding recovers the original information message. This realizes the classical counting guarantee algorithmically without enumerating the exponentially large space of binary words.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gabrys, Shubhransh Singhvi, Eitan Yaakobi

item.title: Hardware-Efficient Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling for Quantum LDPC Decoders
item.description: arXiv:2611.04179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their decoding algorithms present significant hardware implementation challenges. Reinforcement-learned sequential belief propagation (RL-S) improves the error-correction performance of conventional belief propagation (BP) through adaptive variable-node scheduling. However, its heap-based priority management introduces substantial hardware overhead. This paper presents hardware implementations of BP, RL-S, and bucket-based reinforcement-learned BP (BRL-S) for the [[288,12,18]] bivariate bicycle QLDPC code. The BRL-S architectures employ quantized priorities and first-in, first-out (FIFO) buckets to simplify scheduling. Three configurations with two, four, and eight priority levels are evaluated. FPGA synthesis results demonstrate that BRL-S reduces lookup-table utilization by approximately 68--72% compared with RL-S. ASIC synthesis further shows reductions of 63--67% in area and 64--69% in estimated power consumption. These results demonstrate that bucket-based scheduling substantially improves the hardware efficiency of reinforcement-learned QLDPC decoders.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Moradi, Vahid Nourozi, Wei Tang, David Mitchell

item.title: Optimal Communication for Distributed Sparse Histogram Aggregation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Histogram estimation is a fundamental primitive in distributed data analysis, with applications in counting queries and federated learning. In many settings, the universe of categories is enormous, yet each user's data involves only a small subset, yielding sparse local histograms. This raises a natural question: To what extent can local sparsity reduce the communication needed to estimate the global histogram? We answer this question by characterizing the communication complexity of distributed sparse histogram estimation under prescribed $\ell_1$ distortion and failure probability constraints. Our upper bound is achieved by a randomized covering scheme that optimizes how accurately each user represents its local histogram to reduce communication. By exploiting the distortion budget directly rather than imposing unbiasedness, the scheme achieves lower communication costs than standard unbiased sampling and hashing constructions. We establish the scheme's first-order optimality through a lower bound based on local support identification. The key step is to relate communication cost directly to the number of active coordinates revealed by each user's message, rather than to bound information about the aggregate via distance-based Fano's inequalities. This characterization further quantifies how the communication advantage of heterogeneous over homogeneous encoders varies across parameter regimes.
item.dc:creator: Fangwei Ye, Yijun Fan

item.title: Pairwise Distortion Distribution with Graph-Based Importance Sampling for Quantization Error and Intrinsic Dimension Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantifying the dimensionality of data is a fundamental need in machine learning and signal processing applications such as representation learning, data compression, and inverse problems, where the extrinsic dimension in which the data is presented can be very different from the intrinsic dimension that determines the operational performance. Various concepts, such as R\'enyi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension are useful here. Despite their theoretical significance, estimating these measures are challenging given their asymptotic definitions. Recent research has shown that analyzing the pairwise distortion distribution (PDD) of a data source can provide a tractable lower bound on the distortion of random codebook quantization, from which a tractable notion of intrinsic dimension can be derived. In this paper we extend this line of research in three main ways. First, we develop a related upper bound on distortion of random codebook quantization. Second, we improve the computability of both the lower and upper bounds, using a graph-based adaptive importance sampling approach. Third, we leverage the bounds to define new notions of intrinsic dimension which form upper and lower bounds on the R\'enyi information dimension, rate-distortion dimension, and quantization dimension, and which can be empirically estimated from unknown data sources. We illustrate the concepts by analyzing several artificial and empirical distributions.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Carl Nuzman, Shirin Jalali

item.title: Estimating the generator of matrix exponential time-series
item.description: arXiv:2611.04521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The achievable precision in estimating the spectrum of a time-series signal that is promised to be sparse in Fourier space deteriorates rapidly as the spectral peaks get closer together, as soon as we introduce noise. Here, we study the related task of generator estimation: estimating the generator of a matrix exponential time-series and its eigenvalues. We obtain rigorous non-asymptotic precision guarantees on genESPRIT, a practical algorithm solving generator estimation, and show that this task can be solved with precision independent of the spectral spacing. The guarantees are complemented by a Cram\'er--Rao analysis of a relaxation of the problem. In particular, in the case of unitary data with bounded additive noise with effective entrywise variance $\sigma^2$, we show that genESPRIT estimates the associated propagator matrix in Frobenius norm with precision scaling as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sigma NL^{-\frac12})$ in the length of the time-series $L$ and matrix dimension $N$, matching the corresponding spectrum-independent Cram\'er--Rao standard deviation scaling up to logarithmic factors. We prove that the matching distance error in the spectrum estimated by genESPRIT scales as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (\sigma^2 N^3 L^{-1} + \sigma N^{\frac32} L^{-\frac32} )$, which we compare to the lower bound on the corresponding Cram\'er--Rao bound with the asymptotic standard deviation scaling $\mathcal{O}(\sigma L^{-\frac32})$. These guarantees provide the first rigorous bounds on solving the generator estimation problem. As the matrix exponential time-series can be obtained from linearly independent vector time-series by concatenation, this work opens up a new direction in spectral estimation, which circumvents the problem of crowded spectra, under the additional assumption of linear independence.
item.dc:creator: Jon\'a\v{s} Fuksa, Jens Eisert, Ingo Roth

item.title: Mutual-Coupling-Aware Joint Precoding and Antenna Positioning for Movable-Antenna MU-MIMO Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) improve wireless communications by adapting antenna positions to the propagation environment. However, antenna movement also changes the mutual coupling (MC) among elements of the transmit and receive arrays, which affects the performance of MA-enabled systems. In this paper, we investigate MC-aware joint precoding and antenna positioning for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system with MAs at both the base station and users. We establish an MC-aware system model by combining field-response propagation with a circuit-based representation of the transmit and receive arrays. Based on this model, we formulate a weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem that jointly optimizes multi-stream precoders and antenna positions. The problem is challenging because the precoders and positions are coupled through the propagation channels and position-dependent MC matrices. To address this challenge, we reformulate the problem in the antenna-current domain to to efficiently handle the MC matrices and develop a current-domain weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) framework for alternating optimization. Furthermore, we handle the nonconvex position updates within the framework by using majorization--minimization (MM) and solve the resulting convex subproblems with a dedicated conic alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed design improves the WSR over both an MC-aware fixed array and a movable-array design that ignores MC during optimization.
item.dc:creator: Wei Guo, Tianyi Liao, Zixin Wang, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Khaled B. Letaief

item.title: System-level performance in massive ISAC networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.04592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a dynamic stochastic geometry framework to model and evaluate large-scale integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. Base stations are distributed according to a homogeneous Poisson point process, while user equipments and sensing objects undergo localised random motion around their serving base station. Full spectrum reuse with a common waveform generates mutual interference that couples the two functionalities. Communication performance is characterised through downlink queues whose service rates are governed by the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) via the Shannon capacity. Sensing performance is captured by a Kalman filter (KF) whose measurement noise covariance depends on the sensing SINR, yielding a non-classical state-dependent filtering problem. We define system-level performance metrics under the Palm distribution of the base station process and prove the consistency of their empirical estimators. We then prove that, for a typical base station, communication and sensing metrics are associated, so that operating regimes favourable to one functionality tend to benefit the other. The proof combines the monotonicity of the queue and filter recursions in the configuration of interferers with the Harris--FKG inequality for Poisson functionals. We also show that the excess association ratio of the two interference levels decays as the inverse of the network density. Simulations based on a ray-tracing channel model corroborate the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Mengoli (MATHNET, IP Paris, INFRES, RMS), Nahuel Soprano-Loto (MATHNET)

item.title: Non-asymptotic Sphere-Packing Bounds for Finite-Blocklength Scalar Gaussian Multiple-Access and Broadcast Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.04647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates non-asymptotic achievable rate regions of Gaussian multiple-access channels (MACs) and broadcast channels (BCs) in the finite-blocklength regime. By employing a proposed volume-uniform random coding (VURC) codebook that distributes codewords uniformly within an $n$-dimensional power sphere, together with successive interference cancellation (SIC) decoding, we derive a closed-form achievability bound, a scheme-specific lower bound on the average error probability, and a fourth-order asymptotic characterization. The proposed SIC achievability bound admits a simple and analytically interpretable closed-form expression, enabling direct performance evaluation without iterative computation. The structure of the proposed SIC asymptotic bound offers a highly extensible framework, allowing advances in single-user finite-blocklength theory to be systematically incorporated into the multiuser setting. Futhermore, to characterize the performance benefit of joint decoding, we further derive numerical and closed-form achievability bounds for the two-user Gaussian MAC under joint nearest-neighbor (JNN) decoding. Numerical results illustrate the performance differences among the proposed SIC and JNN bounds and existing benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Kaixuan Bao, Wei Xu, Xiaohu You

item.title: Rate-Distortion-Perception Tradeoff for Vector Gaussian Sources with Limited Common Randomness: Exact Characterization and Approximate Universality
item.description: arXiv:2611.04693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The distortion-rate-common randomness-perception (DRCP) theory characterizes how limited common randomness (CR) improves reconstruction fidelity under perceptual constraints, thereby providing an information-theoretic foundation for generative compression. In this paper, we characterize the DRCP tradeoff for vector Gaussian sources with limited CR under the squared-error distortion measure and the squared Wasserstein-2 perception measure. Specifically, we first establish a generalized reverse waterfilling characterization of globally optimal allocations. Second, we derive an analytical upper bound on the DRCP function through sequential greedy allocation of rate and CR. For fixed rate and CR budgets, the resulting representation is independent of the perception threshold. Finally, we establish its approximate universality through uniform performance guarantees: the achievable distortion exceeds the optimal distortion by at most $2\rho^*\approx0.2897$ times the total source variance, whereas the optimal-to-greedy distortion ratio is at least $\eta^*\approx0.7517$.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Wang, Shuo Shao, Ruibin Li, Jingjing Qian, Jun Chen, Bin Xia

item.title: Construction of New Complete Complementary Codes Using Extended Boolean Functions and Permutations
item.description: arXiv:2611.04796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complete complementary code (CCC) is a crucial component in the design and optimization of modern wireless communication systems, particularly in addressing challenges related to interference, spectral efficiency, and signal quality. The design of CCCs is an active area of research, as it directly impacts the number of users that can be supported interference-free in the system. In the literature, CCC constructions are restricted by a set size smaller than the sequence length. In this paper, we introduce a novel construction method for CCCs based on the extended Boolean functions (EBF) that overcome existing restrictions by including a set size bigger than the sequence length. Further, the proposed construction uses functions which are new in literature and provide us with new CCCs. This is also the very first construction where row PMEPR is also bounded by $n$ for a set size in the form of power of $n$.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Prakash, Rajen Kumar

item.title: Linear Equivalence of Full Weight Spectrum Cyclic Orbit Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.04947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the linear-equivalence classes within the two families of full weight spectrum one-orbit cyclic subspace codes. This solves the second open problem posed by Castello, Polverino and Zullo [J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 212 (2025) 106005]. For the first family, the criterion is a fractional linear transformation over $\F_q$ followed by a power of $q$-Frobenius. For the second family, it is an affine transformation over $\F_{q^2}$ together with a power of $q$-Frobenius. We use polynomial spaces over finite fields, the linear-isometry theorem for cyclic orbit codes, and trace duality. The arguments include parameters belonging to proper subfields of the ambient field.
item.dc:creator: Minjia Shi, Ferruh Ozbudak

item.title: The APN Property of Two Families of functions over $\F_{2^{n}}$ from the Switching Construction
item.description: arXiv:2611.05014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $m\geq5$ be odd with $3\nmid m$. Helleseth, Ichanska, and Kaleyski \cite{HIK} conjectured that two norm-perturbed Budaghyan--Helleseth--Kaleyski functions $F_2,F_3$ over $\F_{2^{2m}}$ are APN. In this paper, we prove this conjecture. First, by using the basis $(1,\beta)$ of $\F_{2^{2m}}$ over $\F_{2^m}$, we show that $F_2$ and $F_3$ are EA-equivalent to two functions $\mathcal G_1$ and $\mathcal G_0$, respectively. Their derivatives can be written as two trace equations for a matrix $P\in\mathrm{GL}(2,\F_{2^m})$. We then prove that these two equations have no solution. The proof uses only identities over finite fields, the characteristic polynomial of a $2\times2$ matrix, and elementary properties of Frobenius automorphisms. The repeated-root case and all parity cases are considered separately. It follows that the derivative of each function has kernel of size two in every nonzero direction, and hence both $F_2$ and $F_3$ are APN for every admissible $m$.
item.dc:creator: Chenmiao Shi, Longjiang Qu, Kangquan Li

item.title: Rank-metric intersecting codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intersecting codes are codes in which any two nonzero codewords share a common nonzero coordinate, and they have been extensively studied due to their applications in communication theory, cryptography, and combinatorics. Recently, geometric interpretations have provided new insights into intersecting codes, both in the Hamming metric and, more recently, in the rank metric for linear codes. In this paper, we introduce and study matrix rank-metric intersecting codes. By defining the support of a matrix as its row space, we extend the notion of intersecting codes to the matrix rank-metric setting. Using the slice space associated with the generator tensor of a rank-metric code, we derive a geometric characterization that is equivalent to the intersecting property. This characterization generalizes the known results for linear rank-metric intersecting codes and highlights both analogies and differences with the linear case. In particular, it yields bounds on the parameters of intersecting codes, one of which is sharp and differs from the one in the linear case, together with first constructions. We then consider codes that are closed under multiplication, i.e. matrix algebras. In this setting, the intersecting property can be read off from the algebraic structure, namely the Jacobson radical and the socle. This provides a simple and flexible way to construct many intersecting codes, including codes that do not satisfy the classical sufficient condition on the minimum distance.
item.dc:creator: Martino Borello, Martin Scotti, Lune Vila

item.title: Plotkin-optimal pure quantum LRCs with large minimum distances from NMDS codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) are a class of quantum error-correcting codes that can recover an erased qudit by accessing only a few other qudits. This paper develops a general framework for constructing optimal pure qLRCs that attain the Plotkin-like bound, referred to as Plotkin-optimal pure qLRCs, from Hermitian dual-containing near maximum-distance separable (NMDS) codes. Focusing on a special class of NMDS codes called extended subcodes of generalized Reed-Solomon (ESGRS) codes, we determine their localities by analyzing certain subset sum problems over finite fields. By further exploiting the algebraic structures of ESGRS codes and related codes, we construct four families of Plotkin-optimal pure qLRCs with large lengths and more flexible minimum distances than existing constructions. These constructions provide strong global error-correction capability while retaining local recovery. To the best of our knowledge, they give the first families of qLRCs attaining the pure Plotkin-like bound. In addition, by using the resulting locality property, we resolve in the negative a related problem on ESGRS codes supporting combinatorial designs.
item.dc:creator: Yang Li, Shitao Li, Gaojun Luo, San Ling

item.title: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 32-35 and 37-39
item.description: arXiv:2611.03682v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the kissing numbers in dimensions 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38 and 39 are at least 352320, 370240, 390980, 415308, 499816, 605322 and 768916, improving the previous bounds 347584, 364736, 384836, 409676, 498024, 591900 and 763668. Except in dimension 38, the configurations are those of Edel, Rains and Sloane with new binary constant-weight codes of weight 8 and minimum distance 8 in the middle layer; each additional word adds 128 points. In dimension 38 we add 6855 antipodal pairs of vectors of the second shell of the Leech lattice to the empty equator of Kravatskiy's 591612-point configuration, where 144 pairs were known; this is an independent set problem in a regular graph of degree 11178 on 8386560 vertices. The codes and lines were found by local search, and all configurations were checked pair by pair in exact integer arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Qihong Lin

item.title: Data-Driven Spectrum Access Technologies for 6G
item.description: arXiv:2611.03816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The surge in global mobile traffic, driven by 5G adoption and emerging applications, necessitates new spectrum allocations for 6G systems. With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G. At the same time, the advent of artificial intelligence offers a new opportunity for designing more efficient spectrum sharing techniques. This paper presents four novel data-driven spectrum access techniques to enable efficient use of spectrum for the 6G era: 1) co-existence technique for efficient protection of fixed incumbent receivers within an established protection area; 2) data-driven approach for protecting satellite receivers via control of radiated power above the horizon; 3) spectrum sensing-based fast-time-scale physical resource block blanking; and 4) base station-based spectrum occupancy detection to enable fast-time-scale spectrum sharing with satellite and non-terrestrial network incumbents. These techniques leverage artificial intelligence and extreme multiple-input multiple-output capabilities to enable efficient spectrum co-existence/sharing while maintaining cellular network performance.
item.dc:creator: Foad Sohrabi, Harish Viswanathan, Sivarama Venkatesan, Jinfeng Du, Aliye \"Ozge Kaya, Navin Hathiramani, Pavan Koteshwar Srinath

item.title: Survival-Time Risk Beyond Low-Order Channel Models: Identifiability and Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2611.03871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates whether low-order packet-loss statistics suffice to assess survival-time risk under bursty packet losses, i.e., the probability that no update succeeds for a prescribed number of consecutive slots. Conventional models, such as the Gilbert model, characterize packet losses using the loss rate and mean burst length, but channels sharing these statistics may exhibit substantially different failure risks. We characterize the Markov channels one order above a given low-order fit that share its statistics and analyze their risks under acknowledgment-based scheduling with transmission budgets. We show that, with dense transmission attempts, risk is primarily governed by loss persistence beyond the modeled memory, and the worst-case channel need not be the most persistent one. Under limited budgets, retry spacing makes loss relapse probabilities important and can reverse the risk ordering of compatible channels. Numerical and measurement results show that low-order models can substantially underestimate the risk, highlighting the need for scheduling-dependent channel statistics.
item.dc:creator: Ruifeng Zheng, Zhihan Xu, Pit Hofmann, Frank H. P. Fitzek

item.title: On the optimality of truncation among binary linear sketches
item.description: arXiv:2611.03979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study statistical inference and function evaluation problems in which the input binary vector is available only through a binary linear sketch, i.e., a fixed number of parity measurements. We show that under a certain monotonicity condition, simply truncating the input by retaining a subset of its coordinates is optimal among all linear sketches of the same size. In particular, this applies to distributed testing of correlations of binary vectors when they are of opposite signs and evaluating unate Boolean functions on uniformly random inputs. Additionally, given that truncation is optimal, we immediately have lower bounds for arbitrary binary linear sketches. To illustrate this application, we consider the one-way communication complexity of a distributional graph connectivity problem on $n$ vertices and show that truncation, and hence all binary linear sketches, requires $\Theta(n \log n)$ bits to achieve constant error, while a nonlinear protocol only requires $O(\log n)$ bits.
item.dc:creator: Robinson D. H. Cung, Adway Girish, Emre Telatar

item.title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.
item.dc:creator: Hesam Hosseini, Jinpei Zhao, Masahito Hayashi

item.title: Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete
item.description: arXiv:2611.04444v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Binary prefix coding assigns prefix-free binary words to symbols to minimize their frequency-weighted cost. Huffman solved the equal-letter-cost case in polynomial time in 1952 [Proc. IRE'52]. For unequal letter costs, Karp gave an integer-programming formulation in 1961 [IRE Trans. Inf. Theory'61]. Exact polynomial-time algorithms for fixed integer costs were given by Golin and Rote [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory'98] and Bradford, Golin, Larmore, and Rytter [J. Algorithms'02]. For input-dependent costs, Golin, Mathieu, and Young gave a polynomial-time approximation scheme [SICOMP'12]. The exact complexity when letter costs are part of the input had remained unresolved. We resolve this $65$-year-old problem by proving that deciding whether there exists a binary prefix-free code of frequency-weighted cost at most a given threshold is NP-complete, even when the letter costs are consecutive positive integers $(M,M+1)$ supplied as part of the input. All frequencies, letter costs, and thresholds are encoded in binary. Consequently, finding an optimal code is NP-hard. Our proof uses two polynomial-time reductions, starting from Planar Independent Set. The intermediate problem prescribes the number of leaves at each depth of a full ordered binary tree and minimizes a signed linear score on their sorted right-edge counts. The first reduction represents an independent-set verification program by a tree growing level by level. A fixed-profile identity converts narrow coordinate restrictions into linear penalties that enforce the computation. The second reduction adds large dyadic terms to the symbol frequencies to force prescribed depths. These terms contribute a constant to the weighted number of ones, leaving smaller signed perturbations to reproduce the tree score.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Rishikesh Gajjala

item.title: A Bayesian-Geometric Reading of Classical Model-Based Optimal Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.04450v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical model-based optimal design criteria (D-, T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality) are usually motivated via the Cram\'er--Rao bound as optimizing scalar functions of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). This paper offers a complementary reading in which each criterion appears asymptotically as $N \to \infty$ as the leading-order term of an expected dissimilarity between prior and posterior, with the FIM entering through the Bernstein--von Mises limit. The Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence of the posterior relative to the prior recovers D-optimality (classically known); a reverse KL of the prior relative to the posterior recovers T-optimality (here defined as maximization of the trace of the FIM, following one common convention) and its weighted-trace generalization; and a first-order approximation of the squared 2-Wasserstein distance recovers L-, C- and A-optimality. The five criteria emerge as instances of a common Bayesian-geometric template, indexed by three choices: the dissimilarity, the prior parametrization, and the approximation scheme used to evaluate it (e.g.\ Taylor expansions of the matrix square root). For the weighted criteria, the Gaussian prior covariance encodes the criterion's weight matrix, so any choice of weights corresponds to a specific prior in the family. The T-, L-, C-, and A-optimality derivations appear novel to the best of my knowledge. A sixth criterion, E-optimality, is recovered not as an independent expected-dissimilarity limit but as a min-max robustification of C-optimality against uncertainty in the modeler's prior direction. The framework is extended to distinguish between a designer's prior over unknown parameters at design time and a modeler's prior used for posterior inference, recovering the classical expected information gain objective as a special case.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Tarek

item.title: Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator
item.description: arXiv:2611.04678v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a nearly optimal lower bound on the blocklength of general relaxed locally decodable codes (RLDCs), extending the result of [GGS26] to nonlinear encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. Namely, we show that any $q$-query RLDC $C\colon \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^n$ must satisfy $n = k^{1+\Omega(1/q)}$, closely matching the upper bound of $n = k^{1+O(1/q)}$ by Ben-Sasson, Goldreich, Harsha, Sudan, and Vadhan (STOC 2004). Our proof reduces showing RLDC lower bounds to estimating the output distribution of adaptive decoders. To this end, we introduce a capped Horvitz--Thompson estimator with uniformly bounded discrete derivatives on the $p$-biased cube. We establish its concentration of measure via self-bounding inequalities and control the downward bias induced by capping through a spreadness argument.
item.dc:creator: Guy Goldberg, Tom Gur, Sidhant Saraogi

item.title: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings
item.description: arXiv:2611.04863v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the least pole order of a rational function whose nonzero evaluations scale a prescribed code to a Euclidean LCD code. A residue-one differential yields an obstruction for odd-dimensional one-point AG codes in characteristic two: for $C=C_L(D,aQ)$ with $0\le a<n$ and odd dimension, the threshold is at least $n+2g-a-1$. The obstruction uses alternating Gram matrices and does not require the scaled code to be self-orthogonal. For the dimension-three codes $C_L(D,(r+1)Q)$ on Hermitian curves over $\F_{r^2}$, $r=2^e\ge4$, we obtain \[ n+2g-r-2\le\tau_D(C;Q)\le n+2g-3. \] Consequently the leading genus contribution is asymptotically sharp even in dimension three. On the elliptic curve $y^2+y=x^3$ over $\F_4$, we prove the exact dimension-three threshold $6$ by an explicit multiplier. For repetition codes on the Hermitian family, the threshold equals the general interpolation bound $n+2g-1$. The upper bounds use information sets and hold for $q>3k$, and for $q>2k$ in characteristic two.
item.dc:creator: Rahim Rahmati-Asghar

item.title: A Short Proof and Generalization of the Rainbow Cycle Theorem and Improved Bounds for Binary Even-Query LCCs
item.description: arXiv:2611.05034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A \emph{rainbow cycle} in a list-edge-colored graph is a cycle where no color appears more than once. We give a short and simple proof of a result of [ABSZZ] showing that a properly edge-colored $n$-vertex graph with average degree $\Omega(\log n\log\log n)$ always contains a rainbow cycle, and generalize it to weighted graphs with edges list colored with list size at most $\ell$ and where the total weight of all edges containing a given color $i$ incident to a vertex is at most $\Delta$, showing that $\Omega_\ell(\Delta\log n\log\log n)$ average degree guarantees a rainbow cycle. Using the reduction of [AG26] and the new generalized rainbow cycle theorem, we prove that for $r\geq 3$, every binary linear $r$-query locally correctable code $E:\mathbb{F}_2^k\rightarrow \mathbb{F}_2^n$ satisfies $k\leq \tilde{O}(n^{1-2/(r-1)})$ by showing a rainbow analogue of the odd $r$-LDC lower bounds of [BHKL25,JM25], closing the gap between the best known lower bounds for odd- and even-query binary linear $r$-LCCs.
item.dc:creator: Andrew D. Lin

item.title: Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It
item.description: arXiv:2611.05128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Channel estimators at a newly deployed base station usually start from 3GPP stochastic channel models, which describe no particular street. We ask whether a channel prior pooled from many ray-traced cities serves an unseen site better than the 3GPP CDL models, and whether learned estimators make the difference. With Sionna RT on 14 city scenes, LMMSE estimation from covariance priors, leave-one-city-out evaluation, and pass/fail bars written down before each main experiment, we find in simulation that the pooled prior sits about 0.6 dB from a site-trained estimator with no site measurements, about what CDL reaches after 50 measurements. Learned models added little: at most 0.65 dB in estimation, and in channel prediction a simple classical method beat CNN predictors by 1.8-12 dB from 2 ms ahead. On measured channels from the DICHASUS outdoor dataset (1.272 GHz, three 2x8 arrays on one building) the result reversed: the pooled ray-traced prior was 3.2-4.1 dB worse than CDL. The simulated channels were too clean; with users at the real distances, even a scattering level tuned from 50 site measurements left the prior about 2 dB behind CDL. A pre-registered follow-on on two more measured environments found the generic CDL prior 2.1-4.7 dB from a site-trained one: no further in a factory hall than on the street, furthest in a small lab room. Finally, a hallway model calibrated to measurements by differentiable ray tracing reproduced delay spread, but as a prior in an unmeasured part of the hallway it was 4.5 dB worse than CDL on the full array. All measured results come from one sounder.
item.dc:creator: Krish Patel

item.title: Regret-based Characterization, Information Limits, and the Sample Complexity of Auditing Adaptive Policies
item.description:
arXiv:2611.05227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A policy can earn its performance by where it locates on average or by reacting to information. For any Markov policy $\pi$ in a finite-horizon MDP, let $
u$ be its open-loop marginal, which plays $\pi$'s average action distribution at each step. We show that $J(\pi)-J(
u)$ equals $\sum_t tr Cov(Q^
u_t,\pi_t)$ under endogenous dynamics. Audits based on immediate costs alone can have the wrong sign. Writing the covariance as a joint-versus-product gap gives the bound $|J(\pi)-J(
u)|\le\sum_t span_t\sqrt{I(s_t;a_t)/2}$, with a sharp constant. Hence, an MDP's adaptivity gap is bounded by the information that its optimal policy uses. Estimating $J(\pi)-J(
u)$ from $\pi$'s own bandit-feedback logs takes $\Theta( ar\chi^2 \log(1/\eta)/\delta^2)$ rounds, where $ ar\chi^2$ is an average $\chi^2$-divergence. At the same time, deterministic non-constant policies cannot be audited at all. We also provide an importance-sampling auditor for episodic MDPs.
item.dc:creator: Irene Aldridge

item.title: Efficient Repair of (k+2, k) Degraded Read Friendly MDS Array Codes With Sub-packetization 2
item.description: arXiv:2510.23316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we present two constructions of degraded read friendly (DRF) MDS array codes with two parity nodes and a sub-packetization level of 2 over small finite fields, applicable for any arbitrary code length. The first construction achieves the smallest repair bandwidth among all existing constructions with the same parameters, and is asymptotically optimal with respect to the lower bound on the average repair bandwidth characterized by Zhang et al. The second construction supports two repair mechanisms, depending on whether computation within the helper nodes is permitted or not during the node repair process, thereby optimizing either the repair bandwidth or the rebuilding access.
item.dc:creator: Jie Li, Xiaohu Tang

item.title: A mathematical study of the excess growth rate
item.description: arXiv:2510.25740v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The excess growth rate, defined as the gap in Jensen's inequality for the logarithm, is a fundamental functional in portfolio theory. In this paper, we present a mathematical study motivated by information theory. We begin by establishing its properties and showing that it has rich connections with information-theoretic concepts such as the Helmholtz free energy, L. Campbell's measure of average code length and large deviations. Our main results consist of three axiomatic characterization theorems of the excess growth rate, in terms of (i) the relative entropy, (ii) the gap in Jensen's inequality, and (iii) the logarithmic divergence that generalizes the Bregman divergence. Furthermore, we study maximization of the excess growth rate and compare it with Kelly's growth optimal portfolio. Our results not only provide theoretical justifications of the significance of the excess growth rate, but also establish new connections between information theory and quantitative finance.
item.dc:creator: Steven Campbell, Ting-Kam Leonard Wong

item.title: A Unified Pulse-Shaped OFDM Framework for Chirp-Domain Waveforms: Continuous-Time Modeling and Practical I/O Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2603.14358v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A unified framework for chirp-domain waveforms, including orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) and affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM), is developed. Their continuous-time representations are shown to fall within the conventional Weyl-Heisenberg (WH) framework for multicarrier waveforms, with the root chirp as the prototype pulse. Since the root chirp has constant envelope and is transparent to subcarrier orthogonality, these waveforms can be further interpreted as pulse-shaped (PS) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, whose power spectral density is derived analytically. The derived spectrum reveals that implementations based on the discrete affine Fourier transform rely on sub-Nyquist samples and exhibit frequency aliasing. We prove that the corresponding aliased chirps are only conditionally orthogonal, whereas sample-wise root-Nyquist pulse shaping of the discrete-time AFDM (DT-AFDM) sequence produces mutually orthogonal pulse-shaped chirps, resulting in the pulse-shaped AFDM (PS-AFDM) waveform. We then derive an exact waveform-level input-output (I/O) relation for PS-AFDM over delay-Doppler (DD) channels, showing that the effective channel at a practical receiver is generally not a superposition of pure path-wise DD components. Waveform simulations verify the derived relation to machine precision, while the conventional sequence-level I/O relation for DT-AFDM exhibits a substantial mismatch with waveform behavior for practical channels with continuous-valued delays.
item.dc:creator: Yating Jiang, Hai Lin, Yi-Han Chiang, Jun Tong

item.title: Domain-Adaptive Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding for Image Classification
item.description: arXiv:2607.28907v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep joint source--channel coding (Deep JSCC) can suffer from domain shift between training and deployment data. We study single-source domain adaptation for image classification over wireless channels. A Gaussian example shows that improving channel quality does not necessarily improve target-domain accuracy under a fixed source-trained classifier. We further proposed an information objective to reduce domain information while preserving class information. Motivated by the analysis, we develop a domain-adaptive Deep JSCC method that combines class-wise adversarial alignment with pseudo-label supervised contrastive learning. The former uses all target samples to reduce class-conditional domain differences, while the latter selects high-confidence target samples to obtain class-discriminative received representations. We relate these losses to the information objective, and analyze the effects of pseudo-label errors and confidence-based selection. Experiments on SVHN--MNIST and PACS over AWGN and Rayleigh channels demonstrate improved target-domain classification without additional inference-time networks. The proposed method achieves 98.15\% accuracy on SVHN $\rightarrow$ MNIST at 10~dB CSNR.
item.dc:creator: Yishen Li, Xuechen Chen, Xiaoheng Deng, Hao Zhang

item.title: A Layered Simplex Architecture for Large Alphabets
item.description: arXiv:2608.19908v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A learning architecture induces a prior over its expressible models. Recent work links architectural success to a broad complexity spectrum: model probabilities spanning many orders of magnitude. Understanding how depth shapes these priors and prediction may help explain the success of neural networks and transformers. We study this connection in large-alphabet prediction through the *layered simplex architecture* (LSA), which multiplies independent uniform simplex vectors coordinate-wise and normalizes. At depth zero, the prior is concentrated on the uniform distribution; at depth one, the Bayesian predictor is Laplace's rule. Each additional layer shifts prior mass toward more concentrated distributions. We derive exact Bayesian marginal likelihood and regret expressions using reusable depth-specific kernels. Mixing over depths up to a cutoff logarithmic in alphabet size yields an explicit predictor with rigorous guarantees. For targets uniform on a specified sparse support, the mixture's prior complexity is asymptotic to the support-description cost at every fixed positive KL resolution, establishing a broad complexity spectrum. We also prove a regret lower bound for every label-invariant predictor: the expected description length of the discovered symbol set minus the source's uncertainty about its identity given its size. For Zipf sources in a growing-alphabet regime, the depth mixture attains this bound to leading order. Thus, the symbol-discovery rate determines the regret exponent. Although introduced to study depth, the LSA predictor competes with established large-alphabet methods, including Good--Turing, Ristad's law and an adaptive Dirichlet mixture, while substantially outperforming classical add-constant rules on concentrated sources.
item.dc:creator: Meir Feder, Yaniv Fogel, Ruediger Urbanke

item.title: Distributed Cross-Layer Optimization for Covert Multi-Hop, Multi-Modal Networks: Exponentially Fast Convergence and Robust Tracking
item.description: arXiv:2608.28469v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops the first distributed cross-layer algorithm for joint congestion control, routing, scheduling, and power control in covert multi-hop, multi-modal wireless networks, where adversarial wardens (Willies) monitor radio modalities via energy detection. The Detection Error Probability (DEP), the probability that a Willie fails to reliably detect ongoing transmissions, is generally non-concave in the transmit powers, making DEP-based covert network optimization challenging. We resolve this by constructing the tightest concave lower bound on the log-DEP, yielding a conservative convex problem that guarantees satisfaction of the original DEP constraints and unifies hard covertness constraints and covertness-utility maximization in a single problem. We develop a Parallel Proximal Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (PP-ADMM) algorithm for the resulting cross-layer problem and prove global Q-linear convergence, i.e., exponentially fast convergence, to the set of optimal solutions under standard regularity conditions. Numerical results confirm linear convergence and demonstrate robust tracking performance under channel fading and Willie mobility.
item.dc:creator: Sirin Chakraborty, Andrea Panebianco, Yuchen Tian, Kevin S Chan, Fikadu Dagefu, Yin Sun, Ness B. Shroff

item.title: Confusion-Erasure Bounds of Error-Bounded Decoders under QAM
item.description: arXiv:2609.12631v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: 6G is expected to push ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) toward stringent residual-error tar- gets for mission-critical services, where undetected errors and erasures carry fundamentally different costs. Block error rate (BLER) conflates block confusions (undetected errors) and block erasures, which have fundamentally different impacts on system reliability. To characterize the confusion rate analyt- ically, we consider an error-bounded decoder with spherical decision regions. We focus on square quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) constellations in the finite blocklength (FBL) regime. The confusion rate is governed by the Euclidean distances between modulated codewords, whereas the code structure constrains their Hamming distances. To bridge the two metrics, we introduce a typical distance, which represents the Euclidean distance of a codeword pair at a given Hamming distance on average, and relate it to the Hamming distance through a per-symbol squared-distance coefficient. On this basis, we derive a lower bound on the block confusion rate for random codes and an upper bound for codebooks whose minimum Euclidean distance reaches the typical distance at the non-overlapping threshold. We further characterize how both bounds evolve with the average symbol energy and the block- length. Numerical results, validated by an exact computation for short codes, confirm that as the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or redundancy increases, the confusion rate falls many orders of magnitude below the reliability target, leaving detectable erasures as the dominant residual error.
item.dc:creator: Wenwen Chen, Bin Han, Hans D. Schotten

item.title: Second-Order Image Characterization with Distortion and Secrecy
item.description: arXiv:2610.09472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Image-size characterization relates coding budgets to the probability carried by source cells and their output images. At second order, this relation must preserve the joint fluctuations of active constraints and the information available for choosing an auxiliary description. We develop simultaneous posterior and conditional-composition image bounds, together with cell-dependent reference measures for reconstruction constraints. The reference measures retain both distortion deficits in one likelihood and permit the same analytical description cost to cancel between two image comparisons. A Gaussian evaluation gives matching second-order rates for Heegard--Berger coding with one uninformed decoder in the strict both-active regime, its common-reconstruction counterpart, and the corresponding two-stage refinement corner. The framework also gives compatible helper-image intersections, reconstruction-cell bounds, and conditional-type privacy amplification. An agreed-reproduction image explains when a scalar Gaussian coefficient replaces an optimized information--distortion profile. Gaussian Wyner--Ziv and Gray--Wyner characterizations provide attributed benchmarks and complementary evaluations of the image constraints. For arbitrary helper sections, general reconstruction policies, and reliable-key generation, the finite-block bounds identify the remaining likelihood or partition constraint. The rate applications use the same observation pattern and joint performance event in the converse and construction.
item.dc:creator: Cao Daming

item.title: Seed Recycling: Explicit Codes for Mixed Synchronization Errors Matching the Leading Term of the Gilbert--Varshamov Bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.15631v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Correcting synchronization errors is one of the oldest problems in coding theory. In the mid-1960s, Levenshtein, and independently Ullman, showed that a single deletion can be corrected with $\log n+O(1)$ bits of redundancy, which is asymptotically optimal. For any fixed $t$, a Gilbert--Varshamov (GV) type argument shows that codes correcting $t$ deletions exist with redundancy $2t\log n+O_t(1)$. Achieving this classical GV-type bound explicitly has proved remarkably difficult. Explicit codes with redundancy $O_t(\log n)$ were first obtained by Brakensiek, Guruswami, and Zbarsky in 2016, half a century after Levenshtein, and Guruswami and H\aa stad matched the GV-type bound for two deletions only in 2021. For every fixed $t\ge 3$, the best explicit constructions still require roughly twice the GV-type redundancy: $(4t-1)\log n+o(\log n)$ for $t$ deletions and $4t\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ for $t$ edits (insertions, deletions, and substitutions). We close this factor-of-two gap for every fixed $t$, even in the Damerau--Levenshtein model, which also allows adjacent transpositions. We construct explicit binary codes with deterministic polynomial-time encoding and decoding that correct any combination of at most $t$ such errors using $2t\log n+2t\log\log n+O_t(\log\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. A single construction thus achieves the leading term of the classical GV-type bound simultaneously for deletions, edits, and Damerau--Levenshtein errors, extending the Guruswami--H\aa stad result from two deletions to every fixed $t$ and to substantially richer error models.
item.dc:creator: Quan D. Bui, Shuche Wang, Manabu Hagiwara, Van Khu Vu

item.title: Efficient construction of subspace design codes over constant alphabet
item.description: arXiv:2610.19691v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Subspace-design codes form a central unifying framework in coding theory, connecting probabilistic existence results and explicit algebraically structured constructions. The two core families are folded Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes, both possessing the subspace-design property. These codes reach list-decoding capacity with polynomial-size lists, but their alphabet size grows with code length and hurts practical efficiency. Goyal, Guruswami, and Hsieh achieved a major breakthrough: they constructed the first explicit subspace-design codes over constant-size alphabets via the Alon-Edmonds-Luby expander framework, settling an open problem and showing subspace-design properties can hold without large alphabets. Despite recent progress, constructing subspace-design codes with low-complexity efficient encoding remains a critical open challenge. This work gives an explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r. By comparison, Goyal et al. (FOCS 2026) built r-dimensional subspace-design codes with alphabet size doubly exponential in r squared. Our construction is computationally efficient: encoding scales quadratically with block length and linearly with dimension r in field operations. We use modified algebraic geometry codes, replacing rational evaluation points with higher-degree places to obtain a valid additive code. To confirm parameter bounds, we use Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries. We also generalize univariate multiplicity codes, originally built from Reed-Solomon codes, to algebraic geometry codes, and prove these AG-multiplicity codes achieve optimal parameters.
item.dc:creator: Shu Liu

item.title: The Information Bottleneck and the Privacy Funnel are NP-hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.22272v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a joint distribution $P_{XY}$ of random variables $X,Y$ on finite alphabets, the information bottleneck method seeks a representation $T$ of $X$ that is as informative as possible about $Y$ while compressing $X$; the privacy funnel asks for a representation that discloses much about $X$ while leaking little about $Y$. In both scenarios $T$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given $X$. We show that computing the optimal value $\operatorname{IB}(P_{XY},R) = \sup_T \{ I(Y;T) : I(X;T) \le R \}$ of the information bottleneck problem, as well as its Lagrangian relaxation $L_\beta(P_{XY}) = \sup_T [ I(Y;T) - \beta I(X;T) ]$, is NP-hard. Moreover, unless $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$, neither $\operatorname{IB}(P_{XY},R)$ nor $L_\beta(P_{XY})$ can be approximated in polynomial time within an additive error of order $|\mathcal{X}|^{-(1+\alpha)}$, for every fixed $\alpha > 0$. We also prove that computing the privacy funnel $\operatorname{PF}(P_{XY},r) = \inf_T \{ I(Y;T) : I(X;T) \ge r \}$ and its Lagrangian relaxation $\Lambda_\beta(P_{XY}) = \inf_T [ I(Y;T) - \beta I(X;T) ]$ is NP-hard, and that, unless $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$, neither can be approximated in polynomial time within an additive error of order $|\mathcal{X}|^{-2}$.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Bruno, Ugo Vaccaro

item.title: Deterministic Causal Quantization with Bounded Error: Adaptive Reconstruction and Entropy bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study compression of real-valued stationary sources under a deterministic error bound: every sample must be reconstructed within a prescribed tolerance $\varepsilon$ on every input sequence. Reconstructions are causal, depending only on present and past inputs. Rates are measured by the entropy of the quantizer output, which block entropy coding can approach, and compared with the minimum rate of unrestricted block quantization under the same error constraint. A uniform scalar quantizer with cells of width $2\varepsilon$ is within one bit per sample of this minimum whenever finite-entropy scalar quantization is possible, without density, independence, or mixing assumptions. Under entropy and Sobolev regularity conditions, the gap is at most $2\mathcal{J}\varepsilon^2/(\pi^2\ln 2)$, where $\mathcal{J}$ is the asymptotic Fisher information per sample. Thus the cost of causal reconstruction vanishes at a quadratic rate as the tolerance decreases. A uniform grid, however, cannot adapt to the source. We construct an adaptive quantizer whose encoder and decoder maintain a common finite set of reconstruction values, updated from the transmitted symbols alone; suitable initialization reproduces any uniform grid. When its initial values are at least $\varepsilon$ apart, its rate is within two bits per sample of the minimum for every such source. For sources uniform within separated intervals of width $2\varepsilon$, storing the interval centers attains the minimum and its Shannon lower bound. Such configurations can outperform every uniform grid of the same cell width: over sources with well-separated intervals, the best uniform grid's worst-case excess rate is $1/(2\ln 2)\approx 0.72$ bit per sample.
item.dc:creator: Rama Cont, Massoud Heidari

item.title: The Pivotal Information Criterion
item.description: arXiv:2603.04172v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Bayesian and Akaike information criteria aim at finding a good balance between under- and over-fitting. They are extensively used every day by practitioners. Yet we contend they suffer from at least two afflictions: their penalty parameters $\lambda=\log n$ and $\lambda=2$ are too small, leading to many false discoveries, and their inherent (best subset) discrete optimization is infeasible in high dimension. We alleviate these issues with the pivotal information criterion: PIC is defined as a continuous optimization problem, and the PIC penalty parameter $\lambda$ is selected at the detection boundary (under pure noise). PIC's choice of $\lambda$ is an upper quantile of a statistic that we prove to be (asymptotically) pivotal, provided the loss function is appropriately transformed. As a result, simulations show a phase transition in the probability of exact support recovery with PIC, a phenomenon studied with no noise in compressed sensing. Applied to real data, for similar predictive performances, PIC selects the least complex model among state-of-the-art learners.
item.dc:creator: Sylvain Sardy, Maxime van Cutsem, Sara van de Geer

item.title: Complete Diagrammatic Axiomatisations of Relative Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2603.04530v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relative entropy is a fundamental class of distances between probability distributions, with widespread applications in probability theory, statistics, and machine learning. In this work, we study relative entropy from a categorical perspective, viewing it as a quantitative enrichment of categories of stochastic matrices. We consider two natural monoidal structures on stochastic matrices, given by the Kronecker product and the direct sum. Our main results are complete axiomatisations of Kullback-Leibler divergence and, more generally, of R\'enyi divergences of arbitrary order, for each such structure. Our axiomatic theories are formulated within the framework of quantitative monoidal algebra, using a graphical language of string diagrams enriched with quantitative equations.
item.dc:creator: Ralph Sarkis, Fabio Zanasi

item.title: Bayesian Optimization with Fisher Information Geometry: Gradient Bounds and Trust-Region Methods
item.description: arXiv:2609.31107v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Bayesian optimization (BO) through the lens of information geometry. Pulling back the Fisher information metric through the surrogate posterior map yields a local sensitivity tensor on the input space, which leads to an upper bound on the gradient of reparameterizable acquisition functions (AFs). This view explains vanishing-gradient behavior in high-dimensional BO and provides a common interpretation of heuristics such as RAASP and dimension-scaled lengthscales. The upper bound can also serve as a generic recipe to understand the behavior of new acquisition functions or surrogates in high input dimensions as well. Using the bounds, we also identify necessary conditions for an input location to be an optimizer of the AF for a univariate Gaussian predictive posterior. Building on this analysis, we propose FITR, a trust-region-based BO method that replaces lengthscale-based scaling with local pullback-Fisher weights. FITR is not restricted to GP kernels with explicit lengthscales and easily generalizes to non-isotropic surrogates. FITR shows competitive performance on several benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Saksham Kiroriwal, Julius Pfrommer, J\"urgen Beyerer

item.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
item.description: arXiv:2610.12357v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study two problems: Local Leakage Resilience (LLR) for Shamir secret sharing, and worst-case Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI), over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$. For a polynomial $Q(X)$ of degree less than $k$, LLR for Shamir secret sharing asks what a few leaked bits from each of the $n$ shares $Q(\alpha_1), \ldots, Q(\alpha_n)$ reveal about $Q(0)$. Given (worst-case) input lists $S_1, \ldots, S_n \subset \mathbb{F}_p$, OPI seeks a polynomial $Q(X)$ so that $Q(\alpha_i) \in S_i$ for as many $i$ as possible. Leveraging recent connections between these two problems due to (Sun, Wootters 2026), we improve the state-of-the-art for both problems. For LLR, we show that there is some constant $\delta > 0$ so that Shamir secret-sharing is one-bit LLR (only a negligible amount about $Q(0)$ is learned) whenever $R := k/n \geq 1/2 - \delta$. This is the first result to break the so-called ``one-half barrier'' for LLR, and improves over the previous best known result, requiring $R \geq 0.668$ (Kasser, 2025). For OPI, we give a quantum algorithm that finds a polynomial $Q(X)$ that agrees with at least a $\mathsf{SCL}_\rho(R)-\varepsilon$ fraction of the lists, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, where $\mathsf{SCL}_\rho$ is the \emph{semicircle law} of (Jordan et al., 2025). This improves previous algorithmic (and existential) results of (Jo, 2026) and (Horinaga, Yamakawa, 2026). We also give further improved existential results for all OPI instances; and when the evaluation points $\alpha_i$ are chosen at random, for every rate $R > 0$ we show that, with high probability, for worst-case $S_i$ there exists \emph{perfect} solution. Finally, we adapt the hardness result of (Yamakawa, Zhandry, 2024) to apply to OPI (rather than a folded version); this gives an unconditional separation between the quantum and classical hardness of OPI relative to a membership oracle.
item.dc:creator: Yihang Sun, Mary Wootters

item.title: Optimality of the $D_4$ lattice quantizer
item.description: arXiv:2611.00100v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The minimum is $13/(120\sqrt{2})$. The proof reduces the problem to polynomial inequalities on three secondary cones. We derive the second-moment formulas geometrically and give explicit polynomial certificates that can be checked by coefficient comparison. We also derive a lower bound for lattice quantizers in every dimension at least two from the number of Voronoi facets, using a comparison with circular cones and concavity in the solid angle. This bound strictly improves the sphere bound and recovers the hexagonal value in dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Liu

item.title: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.00647v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We classify the pairs $(q,n)$, where $q$ is a prime power, $n>1$, and $\gcd(n,q)=1$, for which every irreducible factor of $\Phi_n(x)$ over $\F_q$ has exactly three nonzero terms. The positive support exponents of these factors have a common greatest common divisor, which gives a unique reduction by a power substitution. The reduced degree is two in odd characteristic and belongs to $\{2,3,4\}$ in characteristic two; the cubic and quartic cases arise by scalar substitution from the layers of orders $7$ and $15$. This yields necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on $(q,n)$ and explicit factorizations. Among the classified families, precisely those arising from quartic bases have a divisor layer containing an irreducible factor with more than three terms.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhu, Hongfeng Wu
